reason: Seizure and myasthenic syndrome pose imminent airway and respiratory failure risk. Persistent cytopenias increase hemorrhage and infection risk, aligning with high mortality.
evidences: Seizure with cytopenias suggests CNS bleed or metabolic crisis requiring immediate neuroimaging and labs.
Myasthenic crisis necessitates respiratory monitoring and possible noninvasive ventilation.
Thrombocytopenia and anemia demand transfusion readiness and bleeding precautions.
